meaning unsure; possibly: = river that forms the boundary between the world of the living and the world of the dead
man; ◄ son of {L:Arpachshad<SDBH:אַרְפַּכְשַׁד>}; descendant of {L:Shem<SDBH:שֵׁם>}; ► father of {L:Eber<SDBH:עֵבֶר>}
young branches springing from a plant or tree
man; ► father of {L:Azubah<SDBH:עֲזוּבָה>}, mother of {L:Jehoshaphat<SDBH:יְהֹושָׁפָט>}
town; ◄ territory of {L:Judah<SDBH:יְהוּדָה>}

literally: something that has been spread out; hence: = a flat surface on which food has been spread out for eating ◄ usually made of wood but can be a piece of animal skin or leather ► used in private and public occasions, and frequently for sacred uses in the tabernacle and temple
process by which humans gain control over other humans or objects
s.g: to control; to rule; to be in charge; to have power over

s.d: action by which humans or wild animals exercise control over (other) humans, ► and so have the ability to do with them as they please; ≈ mostly used in a negative sense
s.g: to lord it over; to overpower

s.d: causative action by which deities give humans power over objects, ► and so enable that them to handle these objects as they please
causative action by which deities give a certain condition control over a human being ► and so enable it to influence that person's behavior
a flat, usually round, object; made of wood or metal; ► used in battle; held by a warrior in front of him as protection from the weapons of his opponent; relatively small and easy to maneuver
state in which humans have control over other humans or events
state in which humans are unwilling to submit to the authority of other humans or deities
literally: at ease; hence: = state in which humans are not seen or disturbed by others
the placenta and fetal membranes discharged from the body after birth
a person in a position of high authority
state in which someone in a position of authority has given permission for a certain activity to take place
exact meaning unknown; literally: a third; hence, probably: = a relatively large container for liquids
exact meaning unknown; possibly: = a musical instrument consisting of a frame carrying short wires on which small metal rings were threaded, which rattled when the instrument was shaken
literally: third (man); hence: = a soldier in charge of a chariot, but sometimes also used in the wider sense of a soldier of relatively high rank
state in which a countable entity is the third in a range
state in which an entity is one out of three equal parts
state in which a countable entity is three in number

state in which an entity is one out of three equal parts
causative action by which animals, deities, or humans cause an object to move through the air with some speed in a certain direction; ≈ often associated with some degree of rejection
s.g: to cast; to throw; to hurl

s.d: literally: to cast away; hence: = causative process by which humans leave their country because they are forced to settle somewhere else for an indefinite amount of time; ≈ associated with rejection
s.g: to hurl out; to cast away

s.d: literally: (wind) hurls (itself at someone); hence: = process by which the wind blows with strength and causes strong discomfort to people
literally: to cast (someone or something on someone else); hence: = causative action by which humans entrust other humans to the care of a person or situation
s.g: to cast (someone on someone else); to entrust (someone)

s.d: literally: to cast away (one's actions); hence: = action by which humans do what is needed to no longer bear the responsibility for their actions
literally: to cast off; hence: = process by which a plant lets go of its fruits
s.g: to let go; to shed; to drop

s.d: literally: to cast, throw, hurl (something from somewhere); hence: causative action by which humans use force to cause other humans to let their victims go free, ◄ like someone forcing a wild animal to drop its prey which its carries in its mouth
s.g: to snatch (someone's victim from its control)

s.d: literaly: (actions) throw (someone) down; hence: = causative process by which certain actions cause humans to fail in their undertakings
literally: to cast down (a condition); hence: = causative process by which circumstances or divine intervention bring a certain condition to a sudden end; ≈ associated with humiliation
literally: to cast (someone else's) sins behind (one's) back; = action by which deities stop considering (someone's) sinful actions and treat them as something that never happened
s.g: to cast behind (one's) back; to forgive

s.d: literally: to cast down (a construction); hence: = causative action by which humans destroy a building or other construction
literally, probably: to cast (one's) life away from (oneself); hence: = action by which humans intentionally expose themselves to danger to achieve a certain goal
literally: to cast (someone) from (one's) face; hence: = action by which deities end their relationship with humans and refuse to have anything to do with them anymore
s.g: to cast from (one's) presence; to reject

s.d: literally: to cast (a deity) behind (one's) back; hence: = action by which humans refuse to continue to worship a certain deity
s.g: to cast behind (one's) back; to reject

s.d: an eagle-like bird that feeds on fish. It has a white head, chest, and belly, with a dark brown back and wings. It has a dark stripe from the edge of the beak through the eye to the back of the neck and a faint stripe on its chest; ◄ Pandion haliaetus; it is found on seacoasts and near lakes and large rivers; ► unclean and therefore not to be eaten
causative action by which humans remove a relatively large plant or tree from its trunk with a sharp tool
one of the {L:gates<SDBH:שַׁעַר>} of the temple in {L:Jerusalem<SDBH:יְרוּשָׁלַ͏ִם>}

one of the {L:gates<SDBH:שַׁעַר>} of the temple in {L:Jerusalem<SDBH:יְרוּשָׁלַ͏ִם>}
causative action by which humans pull out some items from a bundle of similar items
poetic term = action by which humans take all sorts of goods (including people and animals) by force from an enemy in war
all sorts of goods (including humans and animals), taken forcibly from an enemy in war
literally: (one's) life as spoil; hence: = process by which humans will remain alive as opposed to others who will die a violent death
literally: spoil; hence: = accumulated possessions
process by which a construction is finished
causative process by which humans cause a construction to be finished
literally: to finish; hence: = process by which a projects comes to completion
s.g: to be completed; to be finished

s.d: literally: to complete (a vow, prediction, or task); hence: = action by which humans bring an obligation to an end by fulfilling its terms or carrying out its stipulations
literally: to complete someone; hence, probably: = causative action by which a deity causes the life of a human being to come to completion
literally: to complete (an event); hence: = causative action by which deities cause a situation to come to an end
literally: to complete (what is owed); hence: = causative action by which humans restore what was entrusted to them or substitute it with something else in case of loss or damage
s.g: to pay; to give back; to make restitution

s.d: literally: to pay back; hence: = causative process by which deities or humans cause (other) humans to receive the appropriate return for their evil actions
literally: to pay back to (someone's) bosom; hence: = causative process by which deities cause humans to receive the appropriate return for their evil actions
literally: to pay back to (someone's) face; hence: = causative process by which deities cause humans to receive the appropriate return for their evil actions
literally: to pay back; hence: = causative action by which humans or deities cause (other) humans to be compensated for their actions, whether good or evil
s.g: to reward; to repay; to render

s.d: literally: to be made complete; hence: = causative process by which wild animals are made to live in peace with humans
s.g: to be caused to be at peace

s.d: literally: to make complete; hence: = action by which humans do what is necessary to be able to live without conflict with other humans
literally: to make complete; hence: = causative action by which deities cause humans to do what is necessary to be able to live without conflict with other humans
s.g: to cause to make peace; to reconcile

s.d: literally: (who is of) peace; hence: = someone with whom one has a good relationship and to whom one owes some degree of loyalty; ≈ only used in contexts where that loyalty is unexpectedly lacking
literally: to be peaceable; hence: = state in which humans are inclined to avoid getting involved in conflicts
s.g: to be peaceable; to be at peace

s.d: process by which humans go through difficult circumstances without being hurt
state in which a countable entity is three in number
state in which a countable entity is thirty in number
